questions.cardText:
[Chemistry] How does the pH of pure water change as the temperature increases?
A. It remains constant
B. It decreases
C. It increases
Answer: B. As the temperature of pure water increases, the ionization of water molecules increases, leading to more hydrogen ions (H⁺) and hydroxide ions (OH⁻). As pH ("power of Hydrogen”) measures the hydrogen ion concentration, it decreases. However, the water does not become more acidic, because the relative concentrations of H⁺ and OH⁻ remain equal. In this case, the interpretation of the pH scale itself shifts.
questions.de: Was geschieht mit dem pH-Wert von reinem Wasser, wenn es über 25 °C erwärmt wird, obwohl das Wasser neutral bleibt?
questions.en: What happens to the pH of pure water when it is heated above 25 °C, even though the water stays neutral?

timeline.labelEn: Danish chemist S. P. L. Sørensen introduces the concept of pH at the Carlsberg Laboratory
timeline.labelDe: Der dänische Chemiker S. P. L. Sørensen führt am Carlsberg-Laboratorium den Begriff pH-Wert ein

questions.notes: Wikipedia (pH): the neutral pH depends on temperature and is lower than 7 above 25 °C. Holds up to c. 250 °C, where pKw reaches its minimum and then rises again (Self-ionization of water). Card prints a straight opening and curly closing quote around 'power of Hydrogen'.

questions.cardText:
[Linguistics] What is the study of the structure and rules of language called?
A. Phonetics
B. Syntax
C. Phonology
Answer: B.
questions.de: Wie heißt das Teilgebiet der Sprachwissenschaft, das untersucht, wie sich Wörter zu Phrasen und Sätzen verbinden?
questions.en: What is the branch of linguistics that studies how words combine into phrases and sentences called?

timeline.labelEn: Pāṇini's Sanskrit grammar Aṣṭādhyāyī, an early work approaching modern syntactic theory
timeline.labelDe: Pāṇinis Sanskrit-Grammatik Aṣṭādhyāyī, ein frühes Werk, das der modernen Syntaxtheorie nahekommt

questions.notes: Card's definition ('structure and rules of language') is closer to grammar as a whole; syntax is specifically how words and morphemes combine into phrases and sentences (Wikipedia), so the open question uses that definition.
